A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Discrete Transformer study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original model and extracted-program results in Tables 1–2, training dynamics in Figure 5, and architectural robustness and intervention experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and adds benchmark outcomes, arity and pruning ablations, attention diagnostics, and detailed robustness results.

M1.justification: The default architecture and extraction pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix D adds diagnostic adaptations using an equality-retrieval head class and soft attention with a mean-aggregation operator; Appendix G introduces optional L1 regularization of the output head. These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: V3 retains the original coverage and adds linear_drop, quadratic_drop and damped_harmonic_oscillator to the continuous-dynamics benchmark. Appendices B and D additionally evaluate parity_last3, retrieve_value_by_key and prefix_mean, extending task requirements to three-input parity, key-based retrieval and prefix aggregation.

E2.justification: MIPS remains the external numerical comparator in Table 1, with scores attributed to Michaud et al. (2024). Expanded discussion of Transformer Programs and Adaptive Transformer Programs does not introduce evaluated comparisons against them.

E3.justification: The existing benchmark training regimen and architectural search ranges are retained. Added experiments introduce arity comparisons, pruning and regularization controls, and 25/50/100-epoch annealing comparisons. Robustness tables now report extraction success rates and program RMSE, whereas v2 displayed a training-MSE landscape.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's capacity study and architectural interventions, v3 adds arity ablations, pruning-fidelity comparisons, attention-pattern extension diagnostics and an output-head regularization study. Appendix G also quantifies the previously discussed annealing effect, substantially strengthening analysis of extractability, redundancy and optimization.

E5.justification: Tables 3–4 newly expose extraction success counts across seeds, such as 0/3 and 3/3, alongside mean RMSE. Both versions already specify three experimental seeds and PySR seed 42; no increase in runs or new confidence intervals is reported.

E6.justification: All retained Table 1 scores and v2 Table 2/v3 Table 5 entries are unchanged. V3 adds continuous-task RMSEs of 5.21e-4, 9.37e-4 and 3.18e-4 for linear_drop, quadratic_drop and damped_harmonic_oscillator, respectively, plus extensive diagnostic, ablation and configuration-level results. These are additional results under their respective settings, not improvements to the retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the structural-agreement and discretization-discrepancy definitions are retained. New discussion of arity, bounded depth and attention expressivity is empirical or conceptual; no new formal proposition, proof or derivation is supplied.

C1.justification: V3 narrows de novo discovery independent of human-generated data to recovery of mechanisms without human-written target programs. It specifies comparison with MIPS on shared discrete tasks and replaces claims of rigorous theoretical analysis with empirical analyses. The central architecture, extraction and controllability contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 briefly acknowledges complexity, expressivity and capacity tradeoffs. V3's new Limitations section explains bounded fan-in, possible sequence-length-dependent depth requirements and benchmark-scale applicability. The appendices additionally qualify the attention taxonomy and pruning heuristic, explain arity tradeoffs, and distinguish redundant program complexity from predictive performance.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly explains PLE bin-boundary embeddings and interpolation, and clipped, head-specific relative-position biases applied before masking and sampling. V3 also supplies configurations and the 0.001 regularization coefficient for added analyses. These expand documentation without establishing changes to the retained implementation.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 expands positioning against the already cited Transformer Programs and Adaptive Transformer Programs, distinguishing bounded forward decompilation from compact algebraic program recovery. Reference-list changes mainly correct bibliographic metadata rather than introduce new cited research.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted revisions to the abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion, and adds explanatory footnotes, disclosures and a standalone Limitations section. The main methodological narrative and section order remain largely intact; retained appendices are relabeled around the additions.

P2.justification: The robustness presentation is substantially redesigned: v2 Figure 6's two 3D plots are replaced by configuration-level Tables 3–4 covering three tasks. V3 also adds a pruning table, expands the benchmark tables and reverses Figure 5's temperature axis to follow annealing. Existing synthesized-program figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens empirical support through arity, pruning and robustness analyses, while narrower claims and specific limitations better calibrate the paper's scope. These benefits outweigh limited reporting weaknesses, including terse diagnostic-task documentation and an unresolved discrepancy: Appendix G gives 78 unregularized sum_last2 lines for the 4/4/4 architecture, whereas Table 4 gives 86.
